facts.name: rest_bearer_authorization_header
facts.authored_statement: GitHub's REST API documents that a token is presented to the API in the Authorization request header, and documents two value forms: `Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>` and `Authorization: token <TOKEN>`; a JSON web token (JWT) must use the Bearer form. GitHub's own published code sample for GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues sends the Bearer form to https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/issues.

evidence.quote: Many REST API endpoints require authentication or return additional information if you are authenticated. Additionally, you can make more requests per hour when you are authenticated.

facts.name: rest_link_header_pagination
facts.authored_statement: GitHub's REST API documents pagination through a link response header, present only when a response is paginated, whose URLs address the previous, next, first and last page of results and are annotated with rel="prev", rel="next", rel="last" and rel="first". The published example link header value addresses the listing through https://api.github.com/repositories/1300192/issues with a page query parameter, while the example request published in the same article uses https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Spoon-Knife/issues. The article states that the query parameters in link URLs may differ between endpoints and that each paginated endpoint uses the page, before/after, or since query parameters.

typed.continuation_is_expressed_as: query parameters on the URLs carried by the link header value
typed.header_omitted_when: the endpoint does not support pagination, or all results fit on a single page
typed.documented_meaning_for_pm: A rel="next" target is a provider-supplied continuation for the next page of the same listing; the document does not state that an arbitrary same-origin URL, or any URL on a different path, is a legal continuation.

evidence.quote: When a response from the REST API would include many results, GitHub will paginate the results and return a subset of the results. For example, GET /repos/octocat/Spoon-Knife/issues will only return 30 issues from the octocat/Spoon-Knife repository even though the repository includes over 1600 open issues. This makes the response easier to handle for servers and for people.

must_not_be_read_as: It does not document the link response header for this operation: the parameter table and the status table are the only structured tables the operation page publishes.
It does not license any parameter absent from the parameter table, nor an arbitrary request body or additional header.
The status table lists no 401 or 403 for this operation; nothing here defines PM's refusal classes.
It does not state that the operation returns only issues (pull requests are included) nor that a 404 means the resource is absent rather than inaccessible; only the quoted sentences are admitted.

documented_absences.consequence: For this operation the link header fact comes from the generic pagination article (F2) and from the pinned OpenAPI declaration, not from the operation's documentation page.
documented_absences.note: The words may still occur in the article as a whole; the check is over the whole retained page, which is the strongest form of the claim.

precedence_and_conflict_rules.openapi_is_authoritative: Facts declared by the pinned OpenAPI source set (paths, parameters, media types, response statuses, declared response headers, declared security and securitySchemes) are authoritative for what they declare; a supplemental documentation fact never overrides them.
precedence_and_conflict_rules.supplemental_may_only_add: A supplemental documentation fact is admissible only where the pinned OpenAPI document declares nothing about the subject, for example no security scheme, no authorization requirement on the operation, and no cursor parameter.
precedence_and_conflict_rules.never_contradict: A supplemental fact that contradicts a declared OpenAPI fact is inadmissible and must be refused as a source conflict, never reconciled by preference.
precedence_and_conflict_rules.never_widen: A supplemental fact must not widen origins (the server URL declared by the source), credentials (it may not create or enlarge a credential channel beyond what the operation declares), or capabilities (it may not add operations, parameters, media types, statuses or response headers beyond the declared operation).
precedence_and_conflict_rules.protocol_versus_policy: These facts are provider protocol facts. Connection policy, namely that this private connection requires a credential, is a PM connection declaration and is neither established nor weakened by them.
precedence_and_conflict_rules.scope: The admitted facts cover the single declared operation issues/list-for-repo (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues) only.
precedence_and_conflict_rules.observation_is_not_authority: A link header value published as an example is an observation about what the provider may send. It never authorises replaying a provider-supplied URL, and it does not change PM's navigation rule that a continuation must remain on the declared operation identity.

consumption_contract.admission: A compiler slice may admit these facts only through the approved source admission and normalization mechanism, keeping each fact's quote and locator, and keeping provider protocol facts separate from connection policy.
consumption_contract.refusal: A supplemental fact that would contradict the pinned OpenAPI declaration, widen the declared origin, credential channel or capability, or re-identify the resource address must be refused as a source conflict.
consumption_contract.scope: Single declared operation: issues/list-for-repo. Nothing here generalizes to other GitHub endpoints.
consumption_contract.verification: verify.py re-checks the SHA-256 and byte length of every retained document and re-extracts every quote from the retained bytes at its recorded byte range. A digest mismatch or a quote that no longer matches its locator is a blocker, never a substitution.
